solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plane low in south

indicators.note: in places the cow's sound inside the abbreviation for the compass point

parts.note: STH is a standard abbreviation of south
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A flying instruction: bring the aircraft down low over the southern area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft, but it is the verb used by carpenters.
explanation.definitionFit: To plane wood is to shave it level, which is to make it even and flat.

clue.text: Keen poet's start to day in auditorium

indicators.note: in auditorium means heard by an audience, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: morn is the poetic word for morning, the start of the day

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic poet begins the day in a lecture hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb meaning to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament loudly for the dead, i.e. to grieve.

clue.text: Wide-open rolling pasture surrounded by woods regularly overlooked

indicators.note: surrounded by means the jumbled letters sit inside the other piece
regularly overlooked says every other letter of the word is ignored, keeping the rest
rolling suggests turning over, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rolling pasture ringed by woods lies wide open to view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly overlooked' skips W and the second O and S of the woods, keeping the even letters; 'rolling' is the anagram signal, not scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspread means spread out fully, extended wide.

clue.text: Plant-based starters of rolls bearing filling get better

indicators.note: filling means the letters go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to heal is to recover, get better

indicators.note: starters of picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A plant-based sandwich filling to aid recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: R and B from 'starters of rolls bearing' go inside HEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal means made from herbs, so it describes remedies derived from plants.

clue.text: Develop mock stone to make city

parts.note: to bud is to begin to develop, as a plant does
to ape is to imitate mockingly
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a city out of fake stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, an example of a city.

clue.text: Team of dark and light dogs

parts.note: black means dark
to burn is to light up or set alight
Rover is a stock name for a dog, so dogs are rovers

explanation.surface: A pack of dogs in dark and pale coats.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackburn Rovers is an English football club from Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackburn Rovers is a professional football side, an example of a team.

clue.text: Colouring no good, accepting the old way

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless, no good
ye is the old form of the
ST abbreviates street, a way

explanation.surface: A poor colour scheme that clings to old-fashioned methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is a substance used to dye, i.e. a colouring agent.

clue.text: Boy having time between back-to- back school lessons

indicators.note: between means one piece goes into the gap in the other

parts.note: PE and RE are school lessons; placed back to back, their ends touching, they read PE then ER

explanation.surface: A boy with a free period between two consecutive classes.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education and RE religious education; 'back-to-back' sets RE reversed against PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is a boy's name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: Quiet person massaging unknown growth

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
one who rubs is a rubber, a masseur
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A silent masseur works on an unidentified lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area of shrubs, a mass of plant growth.

clue.text: Admirer of eg diamonds and gold

parts.note: diamonds is one example of a suit of cards
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone who is fond of jewellery and precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, so he is her admirer.

clue.text: Third of Xmas crackers erupt on opening

indicators.note: third of picks out the letter in third place of the word that follows
crackers means crazy, so the following word's letters go wild and get rearranged

parts.note: RE means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: Christmas crackers burst open when pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' is the anagram signal, not the Christmas novelty; 'Third of' takes the third letter of Xmas, and RE is the Latin-derived 'on', meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, a synonym of opening.

clue.text: Brought back kilo, roughly, with tan bag

indicators.note: brought back says the whole string built here is read from end to start

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly
to tan someone's hide is to spank them

explanation.surface: Someone returned with a kilo of stuff and a tan-coloured bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' reverses K + CA + SPANK, making KNAPS + AC + K.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, a kind of rucksack.

clue.text: Three obese Europeans all disregarded pulses

indicators.note: all disregarded says every one of the following letters is ignored and taken out

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, and several Europeans give several Es

explanation.surface: Three overweight Europeans ignore their lentils and beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all disregarded' removes all four Es from THREE OBESE. 'pulses' looks like beans; it means beats.
explanation.definitionFit: Throbs are rhythmic beats, the same as pulses of the heart.

clue.text: Second-rate part of crossword, not the first down

parts.note: B-grade means second-rate, giving B

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: a clue is one part of a crossword

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that a down clue is poor and has lost its first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like part of a crossword grid label; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling down, both meaning low in spirits.

clue.text: Vile stewed meal so hot

indicators.note: stewed means cooked together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A disgusting stew served too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means hateful or disgusting, a synonym of vile.

clue.text: Lacking sustenance, eating poorly and empty

indicators.note: eating means one word takes another into its middle

parts.note: unfed means not given food
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Someone without food who is eating badly feels hollow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfilled has nothing in it, so it is vacant.

clue.text: Artwork drops on head

indicators.note: in a down answer on means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to land is to drop down onto the ground
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A piece of art falls on someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A cape is a promontory, also called a head or headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of scenery, a type of artwork.

clue.text: Learner cutting bandage is excellent

indicators.note: cutting means the letter slices into the other word

parts.note: a binding is a strip wrapped round something, a bandage
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee snipping a dressing does a superb job.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinding is informal British praise meaning brilliant or outstanding.

clue.text: Party on island left in cutter

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the party follows the island

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man
a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party on an island where someone was left aboard a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a boat; a mandolin (or mandoline) is a kitchen slicer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a bladed kitchen tool for slicing vegetables, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: Denials from lousy anarchists backfired

indicators.note: backfired says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The rejection of some useless anarchists' plan went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no indicator for the hiding; 'from' signals it. SYAN sits across 'lousy anarchists'; 'backfired' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nays are votes against, so they are refusals or denials.

clue.text: Searched when missing leader is endangered

indicators.note: missing leader says the word drops its first letter

parts.note: frisked means searched by patting down

explanation.surface: A search without its head guard put people at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Risked means put in danger, the same as endangered.

clue.text: Alarmed fish netted by Poles

indicators.note: netted by means caught inside, so one piece goes between the others

parts.note: the north and south poles give N and S
a hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish caught by Polish fishermen panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shaken is to be upset or frightened, i.e. alarmed.

clue.text: Turf our land all round laurels

indicators.note: all round means turned right around, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: sod is turf
for a British setter our land is the UK

explanation.surface: Turf spread across the country, ringed with laurel wreaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels stand for honour won, which is prestige or praise.

clue.text: Duck errand, showing disregard

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O
a mission is a task one is sent on, an errand

explanation.surface: Skipping an errand shows a lack of care.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to include something, a form of neglect or overlooking.

clue.text: Harangue love cheat with ecstasy

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a rat is a betrayer or cheat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Berating an unfaithful lover who takes drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a pompous speech, to lecture or rant.

clue.text: Gem in bust found outside former pit

indicators.note: found outside means the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
bust means broken, so the words before it have their letters jumbled

parts.note: old means former

explanation.surface: A gem lies in a broken bust near an abandoned mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture but means broken, the anagram signal; 'pit' is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldmine is a mine dug for gold, so it is a pit.

clue.text: Climbers agreed to turn back regrettably

indicators.note: to turn back says the word for agreed is read backwards

parts.note: OK means agreed
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: Mountaineers who agreed to retreat, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas are tree-dwelling marsupials that climb gum trees, so they are climbers.

clue.text: Tangles containing silver wires

indicators.note: containing says one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: messes are tangles or muddles
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver wires get tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wires' looks like metal strands; it is the old word for telegrams.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire was a telegram, so wires are messages.

clue.text: Pass most of traffic getting fuel

parts.note: to pass away is to die

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to traffic is to deal in, to sell

explanation.surface: Getting past most of the traffic to reach the petrol station.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is the heavy oil burned in diesel engines, a fuel.
